MTX-036.interface_type: Three unrelated surfaces under one workflow, sharing no actor and no permission. (1) Schedule policy management: a synchronous authenticated command activating, replacing or disabling one immutable Project-scoped `reassessment_schedule` Policy Artifact version. (2) Execution: an authorized manual start command, or a scheduler-service due-slot evaluation followed by a start only when that committed decision is `admitted`. (3) Cancellation: a synchronous authenticated command targeting the orchestration Evaluation. This is the core of S-18: CAP-020 is the capability obligation discharged inside it and AC-SM-004 is the lineage invariant its publication commit must satisfy.
MTX-036.route: Split by limb, and the split is the ordinary transport answer rather than an owner-decision block. Cancellation is LIVE: API_CONTRACTS.md registers `POST /api/v1/organizations/:organization_id/projects/:project_id/evaluations/:evaluation_id/reassessment-cancellation` -> `CancelReassessment`, permission `reassessment.cancel` with the ID and state version binding the orchestration Evaluation, conditional `If-Match` required, `200`, attributes `ATTR-CancelReassessment` (`reason: text[20..2000]`). Manual start registers `POST /api/v1/organizations/:organization_id/projects/:project_id/reassessments` -> `StartReassessment`, permission `reassessment.trigger`, `ATTR-StartReassessment` with no attributes; schedule activation registers `POST /api/v1/organizations/:organization_id/projects/:project_id/reassessment-schedules` -> `ActivateReassessmentSchedule`, permission `reassessment.trigger`, policy-conditional, `ATTR-ActivateReassessmentSchedule` (`candidate: object<ReassessmentSchedulePolicyCandidate>`). Both of those two carry the ratified OD-025 semantic contract in full; only their physical exposure is deferred to the Volume II transport baseline owned by API_CONTRACTS.md, whose own blocker record already states the semantic contract `is now canonical in Volume I`. Due-slot evaluation has NO route and must not acquire one: it is a scheduler-service checkpoint, and an inbound endpoint letting a client assert a slot decision would let a caller forge cadence that WF-011 reserves to the anchor.
MTX-036.request_schema: Schedule policy command: a complete immutable `ReassessmentSchedulePolicyCandidate` (`policy_schema_version=reassessment-schedule-v1`, `semantic_version`, `activation_mode=immediate`, `rules: object<ReassessmentScheduleRules>`), plus the expected current policy version. `ReassessmentScheduleRules` is exactly `project_id`, `enabled`, and `cadence_seconds`: enabled requires a positive whole decimal integer cadence and disabled requires null, no other scheduling field exists, and a payload whose first due instant is later than `9999-12-31T23:59:59Z` is invalid. No client-supplied effective or expiry time is accepted. Manual start: Organization, Project, actor, idempotency key and no scope selector -- baseline reassessment is full-Project by definition. Due-slot evaluation: the due-slot identity `(project_id, schedule_policy_id, schedule_policy_version, slot_number, due_at_utc)` only. Cancellation: the target Evaluation ID, its expected state version, and a nonblank 20-2,000 character reason.
MTX-036.response_schema: Policy activation returns the one active `reassessment_schedule` Policy Artifact version with commit-time `effective_at_utc` assigned and the prior version superseded. Slot evaluation returns exactly one immutable schedule decision with result `admitted`, `superseded_policy`, `inactive_scope`, `active_evaluation_conflict` or `ineligible`, its exact reason code, and `coalesced_missed_count` as metadata. An executing run returns the immutable terminal Reassessment Result with every field of the Volume I Reassessment Result contract, and on success the replacement `issue_set_id`, `score_snapshot_id`, `issue_supersession_summary`, `recommendation_status_delta` and the advanced current pointers. Cancellation returns the canceled Reassessment Result.
MTX-036.controller: For the policy, start and cancellation limbs only: the registered JSON command controller and its browser twin, each constructing the logical command and invoking exactly one `Workflows::Wf011::Handlers::ActivateReassessmentSchedule`, `StartReassessment` or `CancelReassessment`. Slot evaluation has no controller. A controller MUST NOT invoke `EvaluateReassessmentSlot`, `PublishReassessment` or `FailReassessment` directly: publication and failure are checkpoints of an orchestration already in flight, not request-shaped operations.
MTX-036.command: `Workflows::Wf011::ActivateReassessmentSchedule`, `EvaluateReassessmentSlot`, `StartReassessment`, `CancelReassessment`, `PublishReassessment`, `FailReassessment`, exactly as the APPLICATION_LAYER.md state-changing operation registry declares for `Workflows::Wf011`. `FailReassessment` is the sole terminal failure unit of work for a reassessment Evaluation and atomically owns Evaluation failure, the Reassessment Result, orchestration-guard cleanup, reservation release and the event set rather than chaining `FailEvaluation`. The nested WF-005 through WF-008 stages run under their own `Workflows::Wf005`, `Wf006`, `Wf007` and `Wf008` commands owned by S-07, S-08, S-09, S-12 and S-13; S-18 orchestrates them and redefines none.
MTX-036.command_input: Policy: the candidate and expected current version; the anchor is never client-supplied, because activation COMMIT TIME is the anchor. Manual start: Organization, Project, actor identity, idempotency key. Slot: the five-part due-slot identity plus the Organization and Project states resolved effective AT `due_at_utc` and again at evaluation time. Start (either kind): the re-resolved current policy set, the `reassessment.start` Decision and reservation, the frozen active Source-set version and normalized full-scope hash, and the prior completed Evaluation reference. Cancellation: target Evaluation, expected state version, reason.
MTX-036.command_output: One active Policy Artifact version and one superseded prior version; or exactly one immutable schedule decision; or one new Evaluation created and moved `Pending -> Running` in a single commit with its immutable orchestration context; or one terminal Reassessment Result (`completed`, `failed` or `canceled`). A `superseded_policy`, `inactive_scope`, `active_evaluation_conflict` or `ineligible` decision outputs NOTHING further: no Entitlement Decision, no Evaluation, no Reassessment Result.
MTX-036.actor: OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator holding `reassessment.trigger` for manual start and for schedule management; the Project scheduler service identity for due-slot evaluation and for a start from an admitted slot only; OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator holding `reassessment.cancel` for cancellation. The reassessment service performs only pinned start, cancel and publication actions and chooses no product outcome of its own. The scheduler service has NO policy-management authority, which is what stops a scheduler from widening the cadence it runs on.
MTX-036.organization_scope: The Project's Organization. Every Source, prior Evaluation, Issue, ScoreSnapshot, Policy Artifact, Entitlement Decision and Scheduled Action resolves inside it. Both starts require an active Organization and Project, at least one active Source, the complete active Source set, one prior completed Evaluation with current promoted Issue Set and ScoreSnapshot, no pending or running Evaluation or completed reassessment awaiting publication for that Project, and current Entitlement, Source Scope, Crawl, score, confidence, eligibility and fingerprint policy context.
MTX-036.aggregate: Evaluation is the orchestration root and the canonical write entry -- reassessment is orchestration over a new canonical Evaluation, NOT a separate mutable state machine. ReassessmentResult is an immutable terminal append. The `reassessment_schedule` Policy Artifact is an immutable versioned artifact. ScheduledAction is the durable slot identity and the sole carrier of the schedule decision. Issue, IssueSet, ScoreContribution, ScoreSnapshot and CurrentScoreProjection are written inside the publication commit but are owned by S-12 and S-13.
MTX-036.aggregate_boundary: Two boundaries, and their asymmetry is the design. The schedule decision commits ALONE against the Scheduled Action row: it is terminal, it creates nothing downstream, and it is never revisited. The publication commit is the widest boundary in the product and is deliberately multi-root -- Evaluation, Issue, IssueSet, ScoreContribution, ScoreSnapshot, CurrentScoreProjection, RecommendationArtifact, ReassessmentResult and the entitlement-commit intent all commit together or none does. That width is the requirement, not an accident: any narrower boundary would let a replacement Issue set become current while the prior ScoreSnapshot stayed promoted. S-12's MTX-084 owns the Issue-side members of that commit; S-18 owns the commit itself.

MTX-036.transaction_boundary: Four boundaries, each exact. Policy: one transaction assigning commit-time `effective_at_utc`, activating the new version, superseding the prior and emitting `ReassessmentSchedulePolicyActivated`; the commit instant IS the new anchor. Slot decision: one transaction against the Scheduled Action row writing the decision columns together and emitting one `ReassessmentScheduleEvaluated`; it commits no Entitlement Decision, Evaluation or Reassessment Result. Start: one transaction that serializes the Project orchestration guard, records provenance, re-resolves policy, obtains the `reassessment.start` Decision and reservation, freezes the active Source-set version and normalized full-scope hash, and atomically creates the Evaluation and moves it `Pending -> Running` with its immutable orchestration context linked to the prior completed Evaluation -- creation and start are ONE commit, which is why a targetable Evaluation is never durably visible in `pending`. Publication: one atomic domain commit containing every member listed at aggregate_boundary plus one durable entitlement-commit intent. No provider or network call sits inside any of them; the nested Crawl's fetches occur in WF-005 stages outside every one of these transactions.
MTX-036.concurrency: The Project orchestration guard is the serialization point and `evaluations` partial unique `(organization_id,project_id) WHERE orchestration_slot_active` is where it physically lives, so `only one reassessment orchestration may be pending, running, or completed-awaiting-publication per Project` is true under concurrency rather than true on average. A manual/scheduled race serializes on that guard: the winner starts; a losing MANUAL command returns `F1-DOMAIN-409 / reassessment_already_running`; a losing SCHEDULED slot instead records `active_evaluation_conflict / reassessment_already_running` and is never retried before the next ordinary slot -- two different outcomes for one race, because a command may be told to re-read while a slot may not be replayed. Race winners are fixed by instant, not by arrival: a state transition committed exactly AT `due_at_utc` does NOT make that slot eligible, because an active state must have become effective STRICTLY BEFORE the due instant; at the exact Evaluation-completion checkpoint completion wins and the cancellation is then evaluated in the post-completion window; at the exact publication commit publication wins and cancellation is rejected as `reassessment_already_terminal`. The publication commit re-resolves the active Source-set version and normalized full-scope hash immediately before committing, so a Source activation, disable or removal concurrent with staging fails as `source_scope_changed_during_reassessment` rather than publishing a set the scope no longer supports.
MTX-036.idempotency: Four distinct identities, none interchangeable. (1) Slot identity: `(project_id, schedule_policy_id, schedule_policy_version, slot_number, due_at_utc)`, physically unique as `(project_id,policy_id,policy_version,slot_number,due_at)`. Duplicate delivery returns the ONE stored decision and cannot create another Entitlement Decision, Evaluation, Reassessment Result or event. (2) Command replay: manual start and cancellation use the canonical request hash and idempotency key; exact replay returns the stored terminal result and repeats no transition, usage consumption or event, while reuse with a different canonical request hash is `idempotency_conflict`. (3) Policy activation: expected-version conditional plus the Policy Artifact idempotency identity; a stale expected version changes nothing. (4) Retry lineage: retrying a failed reassessment creates a NEW Evaluation attempt linked by causation ID -- never a reopened one -- and a completed immutable stage may be reused ONLY when its full input hash matches, so replay cannot duplicate Issues, usage, snapshots or events. The entitlement service consumes the committed intent exactly once; redelivery cannot double-count.
MTX-036.background_job: `scheduled_action_dispatch` claims the `scheduled_actions` row for `action_kind=reassessment_slot` and invokes `EvaluateReassessmentSlot`, then `StartReassessment` only when that committed decision is `admitted` -- the job selects no product outcome, it dispatches one. `evaluation_advance` drives the nested WF-005 through WF-008 stages, whose terminal reassessment outcome uses `FailReassessment` as the one multi-root terminal operation rather than `FailEvaluation`. `score_publish` runs the `publish_initial_or_return_reassessment_stage` stage, which invokes `PublishReassessment` for a reassessment and `PublishScore` for an initial Evaluation. `entitlement_reconcile` owns the reservation lease and is S-22's.
MTX-036.queue: `control` (Sidekiq queue `worker_control`, concurrency 5, 30-second claim) for `reassessment_slot` dispatch, which is the queue class Volume II assigns to schedule decisions; `pipeline` for the nested `evaluation_advance` and `score_publish` stages. Queue identity and worker topology are owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row renames nothing and adds no queue.
MTX-036.retry_policy: Not applicable as a slot retry - WF-011 defines none and inventing one would manufacture the catch-up burst PRULE-033 forbids. A `superseded_policy`, `inactive_scope`, `active_evaluation_conflict` or `ineligible` slot is terminal and `is never caught up`; a losing scheduled slot `is never retried before the next ordinary slot`; an Entitlement Block `creates no early retry` and `does not shift the schedule anchor`, and the next ordinary slot is evaluated normally. The only forward paths are the next anchored slot or a new manual command. Execution retry is a Recovery Path, not a retry policy: it creates a NEW Evaluation attempt linked by causation ID, reusing a completed immutable stage only on exact input-hash match. Physical transport claim or deadlock retry reuses the same durable identity and never becomes a new product attempt.
MTX-036.terminal_failure: Nonsuccess mapping is exhaustive and no other customer-visible pair is allowed: Entitlement Block -> `entitlement / entitlement_blocked`; Crawl failure -> `crawl / crawl_failed`; parsing or check pipeline failure -> `evaluation / evaluation_pipeline_failed`; stage timeout -> the active stage plus `stage_timeout`; unavailable score -> `scoring / score_unavailable`; active Source/scope mismatch -> `publication / source_scope_changed_during_reassessment`; atomic validation, conflict or write failure -> `publication / publication_failed`; accepted cancellation -> `cancellation / canceled_by_actor`. Restricted diagnostics retain the internal cause. The Evaluation-state consequence is exact and asymmetric: pipeline failure or timeout BEFORE Evaluation completion transitions running to failed, while unavailable score, Source/scope race, publication failure and accepted post-completion cancellation leave the Evaluation COMPLETED and record only the failed or canceled Reassessment Result. A precreation Entitlement Block creates no Evaluation at all and its Result carries null `current_evaluation_id` and null `current_scope_snapshot_id`. Every nonsuccess records its Result OUTSIDE the failed publication transaction, emits no entitlement commit intent, releases the reservation exactly once, and leaves every prior current pointer and every Current Score Projection field unchanged; an unavailable staged ScoreSnapshot is diagnostic only and never becomes latest or current.
MTX-036.reconciliation: Outage recovery is a coalescing rule, not a catch-up: after scheduler unavailability, compute every unprocessed anchored slot of the CURRENTLY ACTIVE enabled policy whose due time is not later than recovery time, persist exactly ONE `ReassessmentScheduleEvaluated` decision for the LATEST elapsed slot carrying the first coalesced slot number and due time and a `coalesced_missed_count` covering every earlier unprocessed slot, and evaluate only that latest slot once under the same due-time-and-current-state precedence and result vocabulary. Earlier summarized slots are thereby processed and never evaluated separately. There is no per-slot catch-up run, no `coalesced` result and no early replacement slot. A latest slot due while its Organization or Project was inactive records `inactive_scope` EVEN IF the scope was restored before recovery; if a later post-restoration slot has also elapsed, only that later slot is evaluated and may be admitted. After scope restoration, scheduling admits only the first anchored slot strictly later than the restoration commit. Coalescing is metadata on the one decision, never a result of its own.
MTX-036.domain_events: Exactly the ten WF-011 events: `ReassessmentSchedulePolicyActivated` on policy activation; `ReassessmentScheduleEvaluated` for every ordinary decision and for the latest-slot decision carrying coalesced-range metadata; `EvaluationStarted` inside the atomic Evaluation-creation commit for a run that executes; `EvaluationSuperseded` on successful replacement publication; `ReassessmentCompleted`; `ReassessmentFailed`; `ReassessmentCanceled`; `IssueSuperseded`; `IssueResolved`; `ScoreSnapshotPromoted`. Under the ratified OD-025 NO trigger event exists and none may be invented: `ReassessmentTriggered` is removed as a canonical domain event and Volume II MUST NOT serialize the removed name. An admitted run that Entitlement blocks creates no Evaluation and emits no trigger event; it is observable through `ReassessmentFailed`, its linked Entitlement Decision and Audit Evidence. Schedule evaluation creates no customer Notification.
MTX-036.event_payload: The canonical logical event envelope with the real `organization_id`, plus trigger kind; nullable exact schedule policy ID, version and content hash; slot number and due time; due-time and evaluation-time Organization and Project states and state versions; observed and lateness time; coalesced range and count; the eligibility, conflict or inactive result and its reason; the Evaluation attempt, stage hashes, scope and policy snapshots, entitlement reservation, prior and current pointers, atomic publish outcome, retry causation and failure code. `ReassessmentScheduleEvaluated` uses the `schedule_decision` profile: `decision_id` is the terminalized `scheduled_actions.id`, `decision_type=reassessment_schedule_slot`, `decision_status=final`, authority is the schedule-evaluation service identity, `definition_versions` is the immutable Schedule Policy and eligibility-policy version set frozen at terminalization, and it appends `schedule_policy_id`, `schedule_policy_version`, `slot_number`, `due_at_utc`, `coalesced_first_slot_number`, `coalesced_last_slot_number` and `coalesced_missed_count`. No second decision row exists.
MTX-036.event_producer: `Workflows::Wf011` is the sole producer of all ten. Scheduler dispatch latency, Sidekiq claim latency, `dispatch_attempt_count` and transport recovery generation are technical telemetry and MUST NOT be emitted as domain events. The nested stages' own events are produced by `Workflows::Wf005` through `Wf008` and are not re-emitted here; stage reuse emits exactly one `EvaluationStarted`, because WF-007 continues the already-running reassessment Evaluation without another start transition or event.
